question: Mongolian script descends from right-to-left Aramaic and was turned to run vertically. Which way do its columns go?
options: Top to bottom, left to right
Top to bottom, right to left
Bottom to top, left to right
answer: Top to bottom, left to right. The Mongols took the script from the Uyghurs around 1204, and its lines had been turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. The start of each right-to-left line swung to the top, and the first line swung to the left. Chinese columns, set beside it, run the other way.
move: Work out how a thing was made before assuming it copies its neighbour.
trap: Copying the Chinese layout, the best-known vertical script in the region.
source: Kara, Books of the Mongolian Nomads, 2005
reference: Kara, Books of the Mongolian Nomads: More than Eight Centuries of Writing Mongolian, Indiana University, 2005
